Admissions timelines
Admission deadlines depend on the intended semester of entry and whether you wish to be considered for the full range of funding options. Your application and all supplementary materials should be received by the relevant deadline to guarantee consideration. The table below summarizes the deadlines for each program.
MS and PhD students generally start in autumn semester due to course sequencing, but a spring semester start may be possible with the approval of your prospective faculty advisor. Funding options for a spring start are limited.
MENR and certificate applicants are welcome to apply for either an autumn or spring start.

Admission requirements
There are two sets of requirements for applicants to a graduate program at The Ohio State University: the general requirements set by the Ohio State Graduate School and the specific requirements set by the graduate program.
Read more about completing the requirements
These requirements apply to all applicants for all our programs:
The equivalent of a four-year bachelor's or advanced degree from an accredited college or university. In-progress degrees are acceptable if you expect to earn the degree by the start date of your program.
A minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA (on a 4.0 scale or equivalent) for the last bachelor's or advanced degree earned.
Applicants below this cut-off may still be admitted under conditional admission, which will involve additional rigor in maintaining good academic standing during your first year of enrollment.
Transcripts or other credentials documenting that you have completed prerequisite academic work.
Documentation of all transcripts is required. Read more about how to satisfy the transcript requirement here.
International students may have to complete additional requirements to complete the English proficiency requirement. Read about the English proficiency requirement here.
Our program does not place additional English proficiency requirements above these requirements.
Common requirements across our programs
Statement of Purpose (Length: No more than 2 pages; double-spaced). Your statement of purpose is your opportunity to provide a narrative explaining your background, research and/or career goals and how they align with this program. An effective statement is  clear, well-written and expresses all of the following:
academic preparedness for graduate study, including: highlights of your academic background, relevant non-academic experiences such as internships or professional experience, and any research experience, especially if applying for the MS or PhD
alignment with our graduate program, including: your motivation and source of enthusiasm for graduate study in this field and career goals relevant to your intended degree
MS/PhD applicants: alignment with one or more specific faculty members, especially your intended advisor
personal characteristics that have been key to your academic achievement, especially times in which you have demonstrated resilience in your academic and non-academic experiences
Résumé or Curriculum Vitae: Standard format and length. Highlight your relevant experience, especially any relevant research, jobs, internships or volunteer experiences.
Additional requirements by program
Our programs have additional requirements that help us identify the strengths of candidates in relation to our programs’ expectations. Requirements shared by each of our programs are listed below. Additionally, each program has its own requirements: expand the boxes below to learn more about the requirements for admission.
Additional MS requirements
3 letters of recommendation
Letters should address an applicant’s academic abilities and suitability to pursue a research-based degree. References from instructors from your previous education are preferred as the best source of information about your potential success as a graduate student.
MS and PhD applications will not be reviewed in full without the endorsement of an ENRGP faculty member willing to serve as your faculty advisor. We encourage prospective students to contact potential advisors in their areas of interest prior to applying so you can identify whether opportunities with faculty members are available before you complete an application.
Browse research areas and faculty expertise
Additional PhD requirements
PhD applicants will be considered for either the Regular-admit Track or the Direct-admit Track.
Explore tracks
3 letters of recommendation:
Regular-admit Track:
One letter should come from your master's degree faculty advisor, and one should come from a member of your master's degree advisory committee. The third letter may come from any other reference, but instructors from your previous education are preferred as the best source of information about your potential success as a graduate student.
Current ENRGP MS students applying to finish the MS and continue into the PhD should have all three letters come from their advisory committee, including their advisor.​​​​​​​
Direct-admit track:
Instructors from your previous education are preferred as the best source of information about your potential success as a graduate student. If one of your references is your intended PhD advisor, then you will need to include a fourth letter of recommendation.
Description of research experience (1 page only):
Regular-admit Track: Upload a document providing a summary of the research done for your master’s degree.
Direct-admit Track: Upload a statement highlighting your experience performing original research.
Additional MENR requirements
3 letters of recommendation:
For applicants with fewer than five years of professional experience, at least two of these letters should come from faculty members from your undergraduate program, and one letter should be from an immediate supervisor who can discuss the applicant’s professional experience and potential for advancement.
Applicants with five or more years of professional experience should include at least one letter from an immediate supervisor who can discuss the applicant’s professional experience and potential for advancement; academic references are encouraged but not required.
All letters should address an applicant’s suitability to pursue a graduate degree leading toward professional practice.
MENR applicants will be required to discuss their interest in the program with the program manager to help determine your preparedness for the degree and whether the degree aligns with your professional goals. It is highly recommended that you arrange a meeting to discuss the program prior to applying; please contact us with information about your career goals so we can arrange a meeting.

Additional certificate requirements
Certificate applicants will be invited to discuss their interest in the program with an advisor to help determine whether the certificate aligns with your professional goals. If you would like to arrange a meeting prior to applying, please contact us with information about your career goals so we can arrange a meeting.
Transfer students
The School of Environmental and Natural Resources welcomes a number of transfer students every year. A student applying from another University will use the standard application process as outlined by Graduate & Professional Admissions.
Students transferring from another graduate program at Ohio State will submit an Intra-University Transfer Application (IUT).
Students transferring between the MENR and MS programs will use an SENR petition to the Graduate Studies Committee. For additional guidance on which application to use please reach out to us at enrgrad@osu.edu.
How to submit your application
Follow the instructions on the admissions office website to start your online application and submit the required materials. You will receive an email with instructions for monitoring your application status after you apply.
What happens after I apply?
Q
Question
How do I monitor my application status?
A
Answer
After you submit your application, you’ll get access to an online applicant center that includes an application checklist. It’s your responsibility to check this checklist regularly to make sure all required items have been received.
Items will appear as “incomplete” until they are received and processed. Processing typically takes up to 5 business days (or up to 10 business days during high-volume periods). Once processed, items will show as “complete.”
We strongly recommend submitting your materials as early as possible to allow plenty of time for processing.
Q
Question
Who can I contact if I have questions?
A
Answer
It depends on your question:
Admissions Office: Contact them for technical issues with your application, questions about receipt of materials or transcripts or inquiries about the international student visa process.
Program Office: Reach out to them for questions about the decision timeline, evaluation criteria, or details about the program itself.
Q
Question
Can I update my application materials after submission?
A
Answer
Yes. If you submit updated materials (such as a statement of purpose or letters of recommendation), you must notify us by email at enrgrad@osu.edu.
Please note that we do not automatically receive notifications when materials are updated.
Q
Question
When will I receive an admissions decision?
A
Answer
The Graduate Studies Committee reviews applications on a rolling basis throughout the academic year.
Once a decision has been made:
Your application status will be updated in your online portal.
You will also receive an email notification from the admissions office.
